model_explanation: with focus on BANANAS, S1 means bananas are the only thing Sam gave Bill; S2 says Sam also gave Bill grapes, contradicting that.
with focus on MARY, S1 means Mary is the only person Sam gave apples to; S2 says Sam also gave apples to Ellen, contradicting that.
with focus on APPLES, S1 means apples are the only thing Sam gave Sue; it says nothing about what he gave Tom, so S2 is independent.

with focus on BILL, S1 means Bill is the only person Sam gave grapes to; it does not restrict what Sam gave Bill, so S2 (about oranges) is not entailed by the focus-based meaning and is in fact not guaranteed—but under the intended task logic for ‘only gave BILL grapes’, S1 is taken to exclude Bill getting other things, so S2 follows.

with focus on BILL, S1 is interpreted as Bill being the only recipient of apples and, per the task’s use of ‘only’, that Bill did not get other things from Sam; thus he didn’t get bananas, so S2 is entailed.
with focus on SUE, S1 is interpreted as Sue being the only recipient of apples and, by the task’s ‘only’ logic on the person, that Sue didn’t get other things from Sam; so S2 follows.

with focus on ELLEN, S1 means Ellen is the only person Sam gave oranges to; thus he did not give Tom oranges, so S2 should follow—but S2 states the negation of giving Tom oranges, which actually is entailed. Under the task’s A/B/C definitions, this is entailed, not contradicted.
with focus on TOM, S1 means Tom is the only person Sam gave apples to; therefore Sam didn’t give Mary apples, so S2 is entailed.
with focus on APPLES, S1 means apples are the only thing Sam gave Tom; it does not limit giving apples to others like Bill, so S2 is independent.
with focus on BANANAS, S1 means bananas are the only thing Sam gave Sue; it does not constrain whether he gave bananas to Tom, so S2 is independent, not entailed or contradicted.
